supersedes.reason: Records final protocol-gate state and source-boundary revalidation while retaining the calibration reconstruction's factual limits.

scope: Reconstruction of intended qa-gate-codex-run execution from the approved read-only source boundary. It is not a record of a completed production gate run or a controlled-evaluation result.

run_context.statement: The full protocol gate is approved; full screening, corpus construction, and comparative evaluation are allowed, but implementation is not allowed.
No evaluation run, corpus-construction output, or external-review conclusion is imported into this reconstruction.
The 22-file source boundary matches LCI-CSMQG-20260819-001 at finalization.

actors.role: Local Python process that creates state, prompts, invokes a transport, records rounds, finalizes, and verifies.
External process invoked through configured app-server or exec transport; its returned JSON verdict is consumed by the script.
A new invocation with no resume id used for postmortem classification.
Current-user session file described by documentation as a Codex-process witness and read by the QA script.
Documentation identifies a Claude artifact producer/fixer; this role name is not an architectural necessity under the research plan.

timeline.operation: Start checks artifact existence and version syntax, obtains criteria and grounding, writes session state, and begins round one.
For execution, direct artifact-parent siblings are copied into QA/exec; otherwise review cwd is the artifact parent.
The script creates a criteria/threshold prompt, adds rendered history from later rounds, and invokes the configured transport with the recorded resume id when available.

After a response, the script requires a first-round rollout path, records hashes and chain data, saves the round, and finalizes according to history consistency, verdict/threshold, stall, and iteration rules.
A later round accepts only a newer same-base artifact or rebuttal and rejects a transport switch.
Verify recomputes record checks and compares available rollout material, request/response bodies, and available sandbox context before writing verification.json.
Postmortem constructs a transcript and sends it to a new Codex invocation, then writes a classification JSON/Markdown report if the invocation succeeds.

outputs.generation: Documentation attributes generation to the Codex process; no live provenance demonstration is in the boundary.

verified_facts.statement: The local source implements procedural controls for versioning, criteria, chain records, rollout comparison, execution-copy preparation, bounded iteration, and fresh-session postmortem.
The only recorded included regressions passed: four synthetic integrity-fixture unittest cases and a bridge-flush fixture.
Those regressions did not call Codex, resolve the plugin, exercise a live app-server transport, or prove sandbox behavior.
The boundary contains five declared eval cases but no local execution/scoring ledger for them.

attributed_claims.statement: Both transports restore the same conversation and prior direct tests demonstrated recall and forged-history detection.
The session file is a Codex-authored witness, not a gate-written file.
Execution caught a runtime defect missed by read-only review.
A witness rejected a perfect-chain forged session.

inferences.statement: The local architecture is a procedural assurance layer over a shared machine and potentially the same model, rather than a distinct trust root.
Deterministic mechanisms can detect specified inconsistencies and bind records to bytes, but cannot by themselves establish semantic correctness or independent origin of a reviewer verdict.
Portability and exposure depend materially on caller-selected paths and externally enforced runtime sandbox behavior.

competing_explanations.question: What a clean verification result establishes
competing_explanations.explanation_a: Useful procedural evidence that checked local records and a current-user rollout agree.
competing_explanations.explanation_b: Not adversary-resistant provenance where same-user processes can potentially affect both local stores.
competing_explanations.status: Unresolved by the authorized boundary; do not choose either explanation as fact.

competing_explanations.question: What a fresh postmortem establishes
competing_explanations.explanation_a: It may reduce anchoring to a prior review thread.
competing_explanations.explanation_b: It may retain same-model/rubric-correlated error and is not authenticated by cmd_verify.
competing_explanations.status: Unresolved; controlled measurement is required for detection-lift claims.

unknowns.statement: Whether the live deployment meets plugin, model, session, rollout, and sandbox preconditions.
unknowns.resolving_evidence: Version-pinned live run ledger plus raw records and sandbox probes.

unknowns.statement: Whether fresh review/postmortem reduce false passes or false blocks for the artifact classes in scope.
unknowns.resolving_evidence: Blinded fault corpus, frozen scorer, and per-variant results with uncertainty.

unknowns.statement: Whether the rollout-writer attribution and immutability claim holds for the actual deployment identity and permissions.
unknowns.resolving_evidence: Environment-specific ownership/permission evidence or an external append-only/signing trust service.

handoff.allowed_factual_use: Use FACT-001 through FACT-004 and the matrix's verified facts only for local implementation description.
handoff.classification_rule: Preserve CLM, INF, ALT, and UNK labels exactly. Do not promote them to factual effectiveness, independence, cryptographic assurance, or production-readiness claims.
handoff.implementation_boundary: Implementation remains prohibited by GATE-CSMQG-FULL-001 despite full evaluation work being allowed.
